title: Acyclicity of injective finite-torsion coefficients after scalar extension
statement: Let k and K be algebraically closed fields with K a k-algebra, f:X -> Spec k quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and n a natural number with (n:k) nonzero. For every injective etale ULift(Z/n)-module sheaf J on X and every positive degree q, the underlying abelian cohomology of the module inverse image of J on X_K is zero (a subsingleton group). This is acyclicity only for injective coefficients; it does not assert comparison for the constant sheaf or arbitrary coefficients.

source.place: Lemma 59.90.1, applied to an injective module sheaf; Tags 03FD and 03QU supply source and base acyclicity

proof.text: Identify module-valued sheaves with modules over the constant ring sheaf. By abelian acyclicity of injective module sheaves, their positive abelian cohomology on X vanishes. Sections on Spec k are exact and conservative, as its small etale topos is equivalent to sets, so the positive cohomology sheaves of Rf_* U(J) vanish.

All stalks of U(J) are killed by n, invertible in k. Apply the relative field-extension exchange (not an application of the cohomology-invariance assertion being reduced) to f and U(J). Exact inverse image of Rf_* U(J) has no positive cohomology, so the derived direct image on Spec K has none either.

Global sections on the algebraically closed Spec K are exact. Leray therefore gives zero positive cohomology on X_K. Commuting the module forgetful functor with inverse image identifies that group with the displayed Sheaf.H. For n=1 all module objects are zero; n=0 is excluded; X empty gives zero groups. Use the existing coefficient-forgetting inverse-image comparison.
